# What each committed migration contributes, as `db::Lexer` reads it.
#
#     <file>    up=<count>/<digest>   down=<count>/<digest>
#
# The digest is FNV-1a over the whitespace-collapsed statement text in file
# order. It changes when a statement changes, appears, or disappears; it does
# not change when a comment is reworded or a block is re-wrapped. `0/0…0` means
# the file declares no revert at all.
#
# A migration that has been applied somewhere is a fact about that database, so
# editing what a committed file means is not a refactor — the databases that ran
# it cannot be diffed afterwards, which is what makes this lock the only place
# such a change shows up.
#
# Captured when each `<name>.down.sql` was folded into a `--migrate:down` block
# inside its own migration: every `up` digest is the one its file had as a plain
# pre-directive migration, and every `down` digest equals the `up` digest of the
# sidecar it absorbed.
#
# If a committed migration genuinely has to change, regenerate this file and say
# why in the commit message:
#
#     DB_CORPUS_REGEN=1 cargo test -p db --test parse_migration_file
